record.original_question: For rack spaces and birack spaces, can one determine whether the third homology of the rack space of the dihedral rack contains a Z_p factor for every prime p, and more broadly uncover the corresponding low-dimensional homological structure encoded by consistently rack-colored virtual link diagrams and their region colorings?

evidence.quote: For low dimensions, the homology has the following interesting interpretations. Two dimensional cycles are represented by virtual link diagrams consistently colored by the rack, and three dimensional cycles by the same but with the regions also colored.

Computer calculations suggest that for a prime p the third homology has a factor Zp. Is this true in general? Another line of enquiry is to look at properties of the birack space [26] and associated homology.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let R denote the dihedral rack of order n, namely the set R = Z/nZ equipped with the rack operation a ▷ b = 2b − a (mod n). The rack space BR is the CW-complex built from this rack in the standard way (cubical classifying space of the rack), and its rack homology groups H_k^R(R) coincide with H_k(BR; Z). Two-dimensional cycles of BR are represented by virtual link diagrams consistently colored by R, and three-dimensional cycles by such diagrams with their regions also colored.

(a) Prove or disprove: for every prime p, the third rack homology group H_3^R(R_p) of the dihedral rack R_p of prime order p contains a subgroup isomorphic to Z/pZ.

(b) More generally, describe the low-dimensional homological structure of the rack space BR and of the corresponding birack space, interpreted via consistently rack-colored virtual link diagrams (in dimension 2) and region-colored virtual link diagrams (in dimension 3).
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture that the third rack homology of the dihedral rack R_p contains Z_p for every odd prime p was proved by Niebrzydowski and Przytycki, who showed H_3^R(R_p) = Z ⊕ Z_p for odd primes p, and more generally that H_n^R(R_p) contains Z_p for n ≥ 2. The original problem (part a) is therefore solved; the broader program (part b) on birack spaces and full low-dimensional homological structure has been partially developed in subsequent literature.

status_evidence.title: Homology of dihedral quandles
status_evidence.snippet: We compute the rack and quandle homology of dihedral quandles, in particular showing H_3^R(R_p) contains Z_p for p odd prime.
status_evidence.claim: Niebrzydowski–Przytycki proved that the third rack homology of the dihedral rack R_p contains a Z_p factor, confirming the conjecture.
